title: VOID PVP — Loadout
description: The loadout model of PVP_ARCHITECTURE.md §8: "a named snapshot of which mods are on, their settings and HUD layout". An instance of this schema is one complete loadout, the unit that `void-loadout` persists, that Rust sends to Java in `init` and `loadout`, and that Java pushes to the UI as the `loadout` bridge event. Mod ids and per-mod settings are not defined here; they are $ref'd from mods.json so that mods are declared in exactly one place. HUD positions are anchor + offset + scale, never absolute pixels (§8.1).

loadout.title: Loadout
loadout.description: A complete, hot-swappable template. Applying it writes every actuator field and re-renders the HUD in under a frame (§8.2).

id.description: Stable slug identifying the loadout. Used by `void.switchLoadout`, by the `state`/`hud` protocol messages and by the tray switcher.

name.description: Display name shown in the launcher's loadout library and in the in-game loadout switcher.

icon.description: Name of the icon rendered on the loadout card. Resolved by the UI against the shared icon set in packages/ui; not a file path.

server.description: Slug of the server profile this loadout is intended for, or null when it is not server-specific. Purely advisory today; whether servers get a default loadout is open question §16.3.

mc.description: Minecraft version this loadout targets. Only 1.8.9 exists today (§15).

hud.description: Layout of the HUD items this loadout draws.

stats.description: Accumulated play statistics for this loadout, shown on the Loadouts frame.

loadout_id.title: Loadout id
loadout_id.description: Lower-case slug: letters, digits and single hyphens, e.g. `sword-pvp`. Unique within a user's library.

loadout_summary.title: Loadout summary
loadout_summary.description: The reduced form sent in `init.loadouts` and used by the tray's Switch loadout submenu: enough to list and pick a loadout without carrying its mod state.

id.description: Slug of the summarised loadout; matches the `id` of the full loadout.

name.description: Display name of the summarised loadout.

icon.description: Icon name of the summarised loadout.

server.description: Server slug of the summarised loadout, or null.

stats.description: Play statistics of the summarised loadout.

mod_states.title: Mod states
mod_states.description: Enabled state plus settings for each mod, keyed by the mod ids of mods.json. Every key is optional: a mod omitted here falls back to its `defaults` in the registry, which is what keeps old loadouts valid when a mod is added. No key outside the closed 12 is permitted.

anchor.title: HUD anchor
anchor.description: The screen edge or corner a HUD item is pinned to. `dx`/`dy` are measured from that anchor, so the layout survives GUI-scale, resolution and fullscreen changes (§8.1).

hud_item.title: HUD item
hud_item.description: The placement of one HUD mod. Written by the HUD editor (Figma 244:1722) on drop via `void.setHud`, and mirrored to Rust in the `hud` protocol message.

id.description: Which HUD mod this item positions. Restricted to mods whose registry `kind` is `hud`; a gameplay mod that later grows a draggable readout must first be added to `hud_mod_id` in mods.json.

anchor.description: Screen anchor the offsets are measured from.

dx.description: Horizontal offset in unscaled GUI pixels from the anchor. Positive is right; negative values are normal on right-hand anchors.

dy.description: Vertical offset in unscaled GUI pixels from the anchor. Positive is down; negative values are normal on bottom anchors.

scale.description: Per-item size multiplier applied on top of the mod's own `scale` setting. Omitted means 1.

hud_layout.title: HUD layout
hud_layout.description: Ordered list of HUD item placements. Order is paint order, back to front. At most one entry per mod id; that uniqueness is a `void-loadout` invariant rather than a schema constraint, since JSON Schema cannot express uniqueness by key.

loadout_stats.title: Loadout stats
loadout_stats.description: Session statistics accumulated by Rust from the `session` protocol message and shown on the launcher's Loadouts frame (§5).

played_ms.description: Total milliseconds played with this loadout active.

fps_avg.description: Average frames per second across all sessions with this loadout active.
